description: Deliberate sin is the kind you knew was wrong and did anyway. David asked God to keep him from that. So should we.
excerpt: What are the deliberate sins I have made peace with? The ones I keep doing because I have talked myself into believing they do not really count.
verse: "Keep your servant from deliberate sins! Don't let them control me. Then I will be free of guilt and innocent of great sin."
body_html:
Deliberate sin.

Not accidental. Not unintentional. Not the mistake you made when you were tired or overwhelmed or unaware. Deliberate. On purpose. The kind you knew was wrong and did anyway.

David asked God to keep him from that.

And when I read it, I had to stop and actually pay attention to my own life. What are the deliberate sins I have made peace with? What are the things I know I should not be doing, but I keep doing them, because I have somehow talked myself into believing they do not really count?

The little white lie to get out of something.

The gossip dressed up as just processing.

The thing I took because no one would miss it.

The scrolling I would not call scrolling if I really described what I was watching.

The comment I made about someone I would never say to their face.

The thing I keep clicking on that I know is not good for me.

The place I let my mind go over and over that I know does not honor God.

Those are not accidents.

Those are choices.

And David is asking God to keep him from being controlled by those kinds of choices. Because he knew what all of us know deep down. That deliberate sins are the ones that slowly take over. That the more often we choose them, the less they even feel like choices anymore. That eventually the sin is not something we do. It becomes something we are.

That is what he is asking to be delivered from.

I do not want my sins to control me.

I want the Holy Spirit to.

I want to be so sensitive to God's voice that the moment something starts to pull me in the wrong direction, I feel it. Not so I can beat myself up. So I can turn quickly. So I can catch it early. So I can bring it into the light before it grows roots.

Because here is what happens to us. We get calloused.

The first time you tell a small lie, it bothers you. The tenth time, it does not. The first time you gossip, you feel a little pang. The hundredth time, you do not even notice. The first time you scroll past something you know you should not be looking at, it is a little uncomfortable. Give it enough repetition and it just becomes what you do.

And that is where the danger is.

Not just in the sin itself. In the way we stop recognizing it as sin.

We start calling it just how I am. Or it is not that big of a deal. Or everyone does it. Or God knows my heart. And all of those things get in the way of what David was asking for. That God would keep him from the things he could deliberately choose.

Because the deliberate sins are the ones that keep us from the intimacy we could have with God.

He is not far away because of the accidents. He knows we are human. He knows we mess up. He is patient. He is gracious. He is quick to forgive.

But the things we keep choosing on purpose, over and over, knowing they are wrong. Those things dull us. They quiet the voice of the Holy Spirit in us. They start to run the show if we let them.

I do not want to be run by anything but God.

So I am praying this same prayer.

Lord, keep me from deliberate sins. Do not let them control me.

Wake me up to the things I have gone numb to. Show me the corners of my life I have made peace with when I should have surrendered. Make me sensitive again where I have gotten calloused. Let me feel the pull of Your Spirit stronger than the pull of my own habits.

And when I do stumble, let me run back to You quickly instead of letting it settle into something I stop noticing.

That is the prayer.
question: What deliberate sin have you gotten comfortable with lately that God might be waking you up to right now?
